title: A stretchable, electroconductive tissue adhesive for the treatment of neural injury

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The stated formula, DM = (integrated area of methacrylate protons)/(integrated area of reference peak × number of protons in methacrylate group), only estimates a molar ratio of methacrylate resonances to the chosen Trp resonance. It does not normalize the Trp peak for the number of protons represented, nor divide by the number of potentially methacrylatable functional groups per ELP molecule. Therefore it cannot yield a percentage degree of methacrylation such as the reported 18% and 33%.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 3.1, description of mELP/Bio-IL photocrosslinking chemistry
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The paper states that 'methacrylate and cystine groups formed new covalent carbon-carbon (−C−C−) and disulfide (−S−S−) bonds, respectively, upon exposure to light.' The reported ELP sequence contains cysteine, not cystine; cystine is already the disulfide-linked form of cysteine. Standard Irgacure-initiated methacrylate photopolymerization does not itself establish oxidation of cysteine to disulfide. The further assertion that Bio-IL acrylates formed unspecified covalent bonds with both methacrylates and cysteine is also not chemically identified or supported by an appropriate reaction analysis.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 3.1, claimed 1H-NMR evidence for crosslinking and disulfide formation
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The authors claim that disappearance of vinyl peaks and multiplets around 1.0–1.1 ppm 'confirmed' formation of disulfide bonds. Disulfide formation cannot be specifically assigned from ordinary solution 1H NMR peaks in this crowded aliphatic region. Moreover, a covalently photocrosslinked methacrylate network is insoluble, so loss/broadening of solution NMR signals can result from gel insolubility and restricted mobility rather than conversion. No solid-state NMR, thiol/disulfide assay, or soluble-fraction analysis is described to support these structural claims.

Section 2.11 states that all error bars are 'mean ± standard deviation (SD),' whereas the Figure 2 caption states that its error bars 'indicate the standard error of the means.' These are different quantities and the paper gives incompatible descriptions of the same graphical uncertainty reporting.

The paper explicitly reports that only two rats were used: 'one was euthanized on day 7 and the other on day 28.' Four implants per group were placed in each single animal, so the four samples at a time point are technical within-animal implants, not four independent biological replicates. A single animal per time point cannot support claims of reproducible biocompatibility, inflammatory response, or biodegradation, and treating implant pockets as independent samples would be pseudoreplication.

predicted_errors.error_location: Electrical-conductivity measurement and ex vivo abdominal-muscle test
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Bulk ionic conductivity is inferred from a two-probe DC sweep using metallic electrodes, with no stated correction for electrode/contact resistance or electrode polarization and no reported specimen geometry in the conductivity calculation. For ionic hydrogels, a DC two-electrode measurement is vulnerable to polarization and electrochemical processes, especially across −3 to 3 V. The adjacent-muscle contraction test also lacks gap-only, nonconductive-sealant, and field-spread controls; contraction on the other side can arise from direct electric-field/volume conduction rather than verified charge transport through the hydrogel interface.

predicted_errors.error_location: Abstract; Translational Impact Statement; final Introduction paragraph
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The paper claims that the hydrogel can 'effectively enable sutureless surgical sealing of neural injuries and promote tissue regeneration,' reconnect damaged nerve tissue, and support normal neural signal transmission. The reported biological evidence is limited to indirect exposure of an oligodendrocytic cell line in Transwells and subcutaneous implantation in rats. There is no neural-injury model, nerve coaptation/sealing model, neuronal electrophysiology, axonal regeneration measurement, behavioral/functional recovery assessment, or in vivo nerve-repair comparison. These experiments cannot substantiate treatment or regeneration claims.

predicted_errors.error_location: In vitro cytocompatibility section and Abstract statement that the hydrogel 'supported' human glial cells
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: MO3.13 cells were seeded 'at the bottom of 24-well transwell permeable supports,' while the hydrogel was placed separately 'into the transwell inserts.' Thus the experiment tests indirect exposure to hydrogel-derived diffusible products, not cell attachment, spreading, proliferation, or survival on/in the hydrogel. Calling this evidence that the material 'supported' glial cells overstates what was tested.
